result.summary:
Reviewed git diff main...HEAD (commit 6aaa828) for feature/WF02-REQ074-20260822 directly, plus lib/letflow/identity.ex, lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex, the design doc's OQ-1/OQ-3/section-10 text, and decisions/0003 and 0006.

OQ-1 -- PASS, single-member removal at DELETE /groups/:id/members/:user_id is the right port target, no code change requested. The requirement's own text names handleRemoveGroupMember specifically (a single-(group_id, user_id) handler), and no acceptance criterion asks for bulk removal. R-Co's live bodyless DELETE /groups/:id/members route runs a materially different, higher-blast-radius operation instead (inline bulk-remove-ALL-members, main.zig:1400-1430, silently swallowing per-member errors via catch {}) -- porting that as the 'faithful' choice would mean shipping a route whose only real-world precedent is a silent-failure loop, which contradicts the explicit-error-tuple, idempotent-by-construction discipline every other function in this diff follows (add_group_member/3, remove_group_member/3 itself). Read lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex's shipped @moduledoc directly (the 'Group member removal' section, lines 54-74): it states plainly this is a NEW route shape R-Co's own table never binds to that handler -- not merely a pagination-shape difference -- satisfying AC6's honesty requirement. Verdict: ship single-member removal only; bulk-remove-all stays unported, correctly, since it is unrequested and its only precedent is dead code doing something the ACs don't ask for and this codebase's own idiom would not tolerate.

OQ-3 -- PASS, uniform :GroupsManage policy is correct, no code change requested. handleListGroupMembers's PLATFORM_ADMIN-exclusive gate (identity.zig:533) is itself dead code in R-Co -- grep -n "handleListGroupMembers(" src/main.zig has zero route-table hits (confirmed at Step 1b, re-confirmed here), so it carries no live operational precedent to preserve. Every other route in this file resolves to :GroupsManage via one shared wildcard authorization clause; carving out a single handler-local role-literal exception here, with no acceptance criterion requesting extra restriction, would itself be an undocumented divergence of exactly the kind decisions/ records are meant to prevent -- not a fidelity improvement. Flagged forward, not blocking: if a later stage's product requirements call for narrower member-listing access, that deserves its own explicit decision record, not a silent re-derivation from R-Co's unrouted code.

Standard checks: delete_group/2 (identity.ex:435-449) and list_group_members/3 (identity.ex:479-505) are both plain Ecto.Query pipelines (not exists/1-guarded delete_all, join+cursor query) -- no raw SQL, no hand-rolled state machine, matching this codebase's established idiom. Independently re-derived (not trusted from SECURITY-REVIEWER's Step 2c pass) that delete_group/2's single prefix: option propagates to both the outer query and the not-exists subquery. AC6: both flagged findings (member-listing duplication at lines 31-52, member-removal routing gap at lines 54-74) appear verbatim in the shipped @moduledoc, confirmed by direct read, not only in the design doc. Scope: git diff main...HEAD --stat touches exactly the expected set -- two migrations, group.ex/group_member.ex, identity.ex, the router, tenant_provisioning.ex's manifest registration, the test file, the design doc, and bookkeeping. The two pre-existing-regression fixes (identity_migration.ex's copy_groups/2 select narrowed to the legacy table's real 4-column shape; migration renumbering to avoid a hardcoded test-fixture collision) are both proportionate, single-purpose, independently-rationaled fixes, not scope creep riding along. Decision-record consistency: the new group_members migration is tenant-scoped (if prefix() do, prefixed create/index) matching decisions/0003 Dimension B and 0006's schema-per-tenant convention -- no contradiction found.

No GenServer-as-state-machine crutch and no supervision-isolation concern in this diff -- these are stateless Repo-backed context functions, not process/instance code, so REVIEWER's OTP-idiom checks 1/2 (gen_statem usage, InstanceSupervisor isolation) are not applicable to this diff's shape; recorded here as a deliberate N/A rather than a silent skip. Both verdicts additionally recorded, with fuller reasoning, in docs/migration/stage-4-api-surface.md's REVIEWER sign-off section under a new 2026-08-22 (REQ-074) entry, per the design doc's own instruction that this gate's decision may warrant broader visibility there.

No type-safety gap worth filing under docs/issues/ from this diff -- group_members' shape (group_id/user_id FK pair, no status/lifecycle field) has no invalid-state class a struct/Ecto.Enum change would newly make unrepresentable; the design's own idempotent-insert/idempotent-delete choices already collapse the only ambiguous states (member exists/doesn't) into one handled path each.
